opportunities.title: The Bitget Hack Sent a Test Transaction First — And Nobody Blinked
opportunities.why_now: Bitget's CEO just confirmed the attacker probed risk controls with small transfers before draining $388M, exposing a detection failure that keeps repeating across exchanges.
opportunities.angle: Security post-mortem: walk through the 'test transaction' pattern as the industry's most ignored tell, with a checklist of what monitoring should have caught it.

opportunities.title: THORChain Let a $388M Hacker Cash Out. That's Not a Bug, That's the Business Model.
opportunities.why_now: THORChain is under fire for facilitating the Bitget hacker's ETH swaps just days after the exploit, reigniting the 'permissionless plumbing' vs. 'money laundering rail' debate.
opportunities.angle: Opinion/analysis: argue that cross-chain routers built for neutrality will always be the preferred off-ramp for stolen funds — priced in, not surprising.

opportunities.title: NEAR Intents Just Blocked $50M — Proving 'Permissionless' Was Always Negotiable
opportunities.why_now: NEAR Intents blocking funds tied to the Bitget hacker is being cheered as a win, but it quietly undercuts the decentralization pitch every intent-based chain sells.
opportunities.angle: Contrarian take: praise the outcome, question the narrative — if you can block hackers, you can block anyone; map what this means for 'credibly neutral' infra claims.

opportunities.title: A Hardware Wallet Just Got Fooled Without Anyone Stealing the Key — Here's the RSA Trick
opportunities.why_now: A newly disclosed RSA attack bypassed a hardware vault without extracting the private key, a category of exploit that breaks the core assumption 'cold storage = safe.'
opportunities.angle: Technical explainer for security-literate readers: break down the attack mechanics and why 'the key never left the device' stopped being a sufficient security claim.

opportunities.title: Chainlink Adds Bridge Checks Four Months After the $292M Hack They Would've Caught
opportunities.why_now: Chainlink's new institutional bridge-check tooling arrives months after the Kelp exploit it's designed to prevent — a familiar 'security after the fire' timeline.
opportunities.angle: Pattern piece: catalog how bridge security tooling in crypto is consistently reactive, using Kelp as the latest data point in a timeline of preventable losses.
